% table — a ruled table's cell text, in reading order.
%
% One concern, and it is deliberately the smaller half of the problem: does every
% cell's text come out, once, with rows kept together? Grid emission is a documented
% debt (DESIGN.md §10), so the gold file asserts the text and its row grouping
% rather than pipes and dashes. When that debt is paid the gold file changes; what
% it must never permit is a cell going missing or two cells merging, which is the
% failure a table's column gaps actually produce — the space inference sees a gap
% wide enough to be a paragraph break and splits a row, or narrow enough to be a
% word and joins two cells.
%
% Rules on every edge, because a ruled table is the case a layout reader can
% recognize from its strokes. Three columns and three rows: two of either cannot
% distinguish a transposed read from a correct one.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\pagestyle{empty}
\begin{document}

\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|}
\hline
Header A & Header B & Header C \\
\hline
Cell A1 & Cell B1 & Cell C1 \\
\hline
Cell A2 & Cell B2 & Cell C2 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

\end{document}
